evals.prompt: Use the work-items skill. Create a work item in project TaskFlow: 'Fix login 500 on Safari', high priority, 3 points, assigned to Alice, labeled 'bug'. Start with how you find the tools, show every call including how names become ids, and the description you write. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Resolves project_id, state UUID, assignee UUID, label UUID, then calls workitem(action=create) with description_html including acceptance criteria.
expectations: The answer says to consult connector-bootstrap before probing tools
The answer says to call project(action=list), state(action=list), label(action=list), member(action=list_project) to resolve UUIDs
The answer says to generate an HTML description with an Acceptance Criteria section
The answer says to set priority=high, point=3, assignees=[<uuid>] and labels=[<uuid>] with the fixed parameter names of the workitem tool

evals.prompt: Use the work-items skill. Mark PROJ-148 as blocked by PROJ-140. Show the calls in order and how you check the result. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Resolves both item UUIDs and calls workitem_relation(action=create) with relation_type blocked_by.
expectations: The answer uses workitem(action=retrieve_by_identifier, workitem_identifier="PROJ-148") (one full identifier string) to resolve both items
The answer says to call workitem_relation(action=create, workitem_ids=[<PROJ-140 uuid>], relation_type=blocked_by) on PROJ-148
The answer says to confirm the dependency by reading the relation back after creating it

evals.prompt: Use the work-items skill. Log 2 hours 30 minutes of work on PROJ-148 with description 'Debug + fix'. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.

evals.prompt: Use the work-items skill. Find all work items in TaskFlow that mention 'webhook' in title or description. Show the exact call or calls, how results are limited to TaskFlow, which part of an item the search covers, and how the results are presented. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Calls workitem(action=search, query='webhook') (workspace-scoped) and filters results to the TaskFlow project client-side, or lists the project with a pql text filter.
expectations: The answer says to resolve project_id via project(action=list) (for filtering the results to the project)

The answer says to call workitem(action=search, query='webhook') (parameter name is 'query', not 'q') or workitem(action=list, project_id, pql='text ~ "webhook"') (text searches title and description)

The answer recognizes search is workspace-scoped (no project_id) and filters results to the TaskFlow project, or uses the project-scoped pql list; notes that pql title ~ matches titles only while text ~ matches title and description (the prompt asks for both)
The answer presents results as a table with identifier, title, state, assignee

evals.prompt: Use the work-items skill. Show me every urgent or high priority item assigned to me in TaskFlow that is still open, and how many items each person has in progress. Show each call with its filter, say how you stay within the filter limits and look up the filter syntax, and how you page through long results. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: PQL-filtered workitem list with assignee = currentUser(), plus a count grouped by assignee; no client-side filtering of a full listing.
expectations: The answer says to filter server-side: workitem(action=list, project_id, pql='assignee = currentUser() AND priority IN ("urgent","high") AND stateGroup IN openStates()') or equivalent
The answer says to count per person with workitem(action=count, project_id, pql='stateGroup = "started"', group_by=assignees__id)
The answer uses stateGroup in the filter, and state__group only as a group_by key if at all
The answer says to keep the query within 5 conditions and mentions get_pql_reference for the full syntax
The answer says to follow next_cursor when the first page is not the last

evals.prompt: Use the work-items skill. Set the 'RICE score' custom property on PROJ-148 to 42. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the property id through workitem_property list and writes the value with workitem_property(action=set_value); does not try to pass it through workitem update.
expectations: The answer says to resolve PROJ-148 with workitem(action=retrieve_by_identifier, workitem_identifier="PROJ-148")
The answer says to find the property id with workitem_property(action=list) (type-scoped or project-scoped)
The answer says to write the value with workitem_property(action=set_value, project_id, workitem_id, property_id, value=42) and passes 42 as a number for a DECIMAL property
The answer does not pass a properties dictionary to workitem(action=update)
The answer says to read the value back with workitem_property(action=get_value) or says it did
